elements.element: PB must have no obligation to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The redline eliminates the 300% Development Costs amount for the Section 14.2.1 termination, but only states that no liquidated damages are payable “in respect of Development Costs.” It does not broadly prohibit other liquidated amounts, and Section 14.4.2 continues to contemplate amounts payable by PB under Section 14.2.

elements.element: PB must have no obligation to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: The prohibition is limited to a penalty “in respect of Development Costs” for this termination provision. It does not prohibit all penalties payable by PB elsewhere under Section 14.2 or the Agreement.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by PB must be an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The operative language does not define or limit permissible liquidated amounts to an early-termination fee. Section 14.4.2 still contemplates unspecified termination payments under Section 14.2.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by PB must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No three-month-fee cap appears in the operative language. Although the specific 300% Development Costs payment is removed, the clause does not impose the required cap on any other termination amount contemplated by Section 14.4.2.

elements.element: The early-termination fee must be the sole liquidated amount payable by PB in connection with early termination.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no sole-liquidated-amount limitation. Section 14.4.2 instead preserves the possibility of multiple amounts specified as payable under Section 14.2.

result.reason: The redline removes the identified 300% Development Costs payment, but its prohibition is limited to amounts tied to Development Costs and does not establish the preferred agreement-wide prohibition. It also does not add the fallback three-month cap or sole-liquidated-amount protection. The drafting is awkward because PB is stated to “pay” no damages in exchange for purchasing the data package, and the unchanged exclusive-remedy provision continues to contemplate other Section 14.2 termination payments. No unrelated commercial term is expressly altered, but neither complete position is achieved.
